haiku-low.q1: After the build and migration check, before any new-release instance exists, a single migrate task runs. The live colour must keep working on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using it has been retired, meaning its env was scaled down in the retire step of the deploy that replaced it.
haiku-low.q3: All four instances must pass /healthz three times in a row, then the smoke suite must pass via the test listener. If not before gate_deadline (now plus 10 min), abort.
haiku-low.q4: An engineer or pipeline flips the prod listener to the candidate's target group in one unweighted change, after smoke passes. The previous env keeps running.
haiku-low.q5: Public-listener 5xx above 1% over a rolling 5-minute window, during the 15-minute watch from T. Rollback repoints the listener to standby, scales new env to 0, alerts. Migrations and old env are untouched.
haiku-low.q6: Back to the old colour until retire at T+30, when it is scaled to 0. After that there is no quick flip back; a problem needs a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: A failed transaction rolls back, leaving the schema unchanged. A failed index build drops its invalid index; committed tables and columns stay. The run stops, the new side never starts, live keeps serving, and the deploy finishes failed.
haiku-low.q8: The public listener's forward target determines the live colour; it is the only lasting record, with no state file. The run copies it into live_colour and new_colour, and the other colour receives the release.
haiku-low.q9: The deploy-catalog-web concurrency group; other deploys queue. A deploy holds it until finish, and a dead run is released by CI.
haiku-low.q10: Through the internal test listener on port 8443, reachable only from CI, pointed at the candidate's target group. Smoke runs after health passes, while users are still on the old env.
haiku-low.q11: The pipeline runs a single migrate task from the new image against the shared Postgres. Instances do not migrate on boot, so it runs once per deploy.
haiku-low.q12: After an abort or rollback, the new colour is scaled to 0 and left idle and empty. The next deploy goes into whichever colour has 0 instances; the live-colour step scales down any leftover instances.

sonnet.q1: After the flip and the watch-independent steps? No: per the document, migrations run in the Migrations step before any instance of the new release exists; the live (old) colour must keep working on the migrated schema (changes are additive). Exact ordering relative to the flip checklist item is ambiguous in the list, but the doc says it happens before any new-release instance exists.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still uses the thing has been retired (its env scaled down in the retire step of the deploy that replaced it). The build-step check rejects pending migrations that drop, rename or change type of a column/table.
sonnet.q3: It must bring up 4 instances that all pass /healthz 3 times in a row (checked every 10s), then pass the smoke suite via the test listener, all within gate_deadline (now + 10 min). If health or smoke fails or the deadline runs out, abort: scale candidate to 0, leave prod listener alone, finish as failed.
sonnet.q4: By one change that flips the prod listener to the candidate's target group, all at once, nothing weighted; in-flight requests on the old env just finish. Only done after smoke passed within the gate deadline.
sonnet.q5: Automatic rollback is triggered when 5xx on the public listener (rolling 5 min window) exceeds 1% during the 15 min watch from T. Rollback points the listener back at the standby colour's target group, scales the new env to 0, and alerts. It never touches migrations (schema stays as is). If repointing fails it retries every 10s, pages on-call, holds the slot, then finishes as failed.
sonnet.q6: Until retire at T+30 (counted from switched_at), when the previous colour is scaled to 0. Between T+15 and T+30 the standby is still up and an engineer can trigger the pipeline's rollback job. After T+30 there is no quick flip back; a rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release through the whole process again.
sonnet.q7: If the table/column transaction fails, it rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, the task drops the invalid index; committed table/column changes stay (additive), and the failed index isn't recorded so the next deploy retries it. Either way the run stops, the new side is never started, live keeps serving, and the run finishes as failed.
sonnet.q8: By looking at where the public listener forwards, which is the only lasting record (no state file). The run copies it into run variables live_colour and new_colour (which exist only for the run). The other colour receives the new release; if it still has instances it is scaled to 0 first.
sonnet.q9: A concurrency group (deploy slot/lock) named deploy-catalog-web; others queue. It is held from the start of the run right through to Finish, where it is released (also released by CI if the run dies, e.g. lost runner or cancelled).
sonnet.q10: Through an internal test listener on port 8443, reachable only from CI, pointed at the candidate's target group, after health passes. Users stay on the old env via the prod listener.
sonnet.q11: A single `migrate` task run from the new image against the shared Postgres. Instances do not migrate on boot, which keeps it to once per deploy.
sonnet.q12: They are scaled to 0 (idle and empty). The colour at 0 instances is the one the next deploy goes into; if the scale-down failed on abort, an alert fires and the next deploy's live-colour step scales it to 0.
